claims.text: Replacing an EAM reference with an MLIP trained on diverse ab initio solid and liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in high-entropy alloys at high temperature.
Replacing the EAM reference with such an MLIP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed approach applies to multicomponent HEAs with five or more principal elements, including equiatomic refractory alloys.
An MLIP, such as a neural-network potential or Gaussian Approximation Potential, should be used as the reference model in thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method is applicable at approximately 0.9–1.0 times the melting temperature.
Near melting, HEA liquids display a large diversity of atomic configurations.
An MLIP can capture a broader set of atomic environments than the simplified many-body form of EAM.
The additional environments captured by the MLIP are especially relevant to the disordered liquid state.
Training on ab initio solid and liquid configurations will allow the MLIP to reproduce the ab initio potential-energy surface more accurately.
More accurate reproduction of the ab initio potential-energy surface will enhance phase-space overlap with the target system.
Improved phase-space overlap will shorten and smooth the thermodynamic-integration path.
The MLIP reference is preliminarily predicted to reduce integration-path mismatch by about 50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Reducing integration-path mismatch will produce more reliable free-energy estimates.
Current TOR-TILD EAM references inadequately represent diverse liquid configurations.
The inadequate representation of liquid configurations by EAM references causes significant mismatch between the reference and ab initio potentials along the integration path.
MLIP performance may degrade for compositions or temperatures outside its training set.
Extreme local fluctuations in highly disordered states may remain difficult for the MLIP.
The MLIP and EAM references can be compared against an ab initio free-energy benchmark over temperatures near melting.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction of approximately 30–50% in path mismatch relative to EAM would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of MLIP-derived free energies to converge more closely than EAM-derived values to the ab initio benchmark would falsify the hypothesis.
